title: From Every Stormy Wind That Blows
description: From Every Stormy Wind That Blows in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Hugh Stowell wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 452 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Mercy-seat”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From ev-ery storm-y wind that blows, From ev-ery swel-ling tide of woes, There is a calm, a sure re-treat; 'Tis found be-fore the mer-cy seat.

lines: From every stormy wind that blows,
From every swelling tide of woes,
There is a calm, a sure retreat;
There is a place were Jesus sheds
The oil of gladness on our heads, —
A place of all on earth most sweet;
There is a scene where spirits blend,
Where friend holds fellowship with friend;
Though sundered far, by faith they meet
There, there, on eagle wings we soar,
And sin and sense molest no more;
And heaven comes down our souls to greet,

licence: Public domain: Hugh Stowell died in 1865.
credits: Words by Hugh Stowell (1799–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
